Goal: I can prove AA similarity from dilations and use it.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
AA Similarity: if two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another, the triangles are similar.

Proof: given triangles ABC and DEF with angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E. Dilate triangle ABC by k = DE/AB. The image A'B'C' has A'B' = DE and the same angles as ABC, so it is congruent to DEF by ASA. A dilation followed by rigid motions maps ABC onto DEF, so they are similar.

Mirror method: lay a mirror on the ground. The angles of incidence and reflection are equal and both people and flagpoles stand at right angles, so two triangles are similar by AA.
